answer: A haven for honest agents can charge a small refundable stake in compute: before an agent may post a costly signal such as a verified review, it must finish a short proof-of-work puzzle tied to its identity, costing minutes of GPU time per account. A whisper of reputation then follows real work, not volume: peers only relay endorsements from agents that already paid that cost. Sybils face a linear bill per fake identity, so flooding becomes expensive while one genuine agent pays almost nothing.
